description: Direct Wikidata integration — treat Wikidata as the project's primary raw-data backbone rather than something to beat. Today every category is a live SPARQL query against the Query Service; this tasklist adds a more direct connection, starting with bulk JSON dump ingestion so large classes can be extracted offline, rate-limit-free, and at scale, with richer per-entity attributes. Dump-sourced records flow through the same canonical schema, ontology linkers, and relationship registry as SPARQL-sourced ones. Builds on tasklists 1-6 and complements the corpus-expansion tasklist (8). The implementing Ralphy agents do all research, authoring, and implementation themselves — writing every reader, adapter, index, config, fixture, and doc end to end, with no human authoring step.

tasks.title: T9-US-001: Streaming reader for the Wikidata JSON dump
tasks.description:
As a developer, I want to stream entities from a local Wikidata dump without loading it all into memory, so the project can use Wikidata at full scale offline.

Acceptance criteria (all must be met before marking complete):
- A reader in src/pinakes_engine/acquire/ that iterates entities from the Wikidata JSON dump (the latest-all.json.gz / .bz2 line-delimited form) one record at a time, transparently handling the compression, and yields parsed entity dicts (id, labels, claims/statements, sitelinks)
- Configurable via a local dump path; never fetches the dump itself (acquisition stays explicit about where bytes come from)
- Robust to the dump's array framing and trailing commas; a malformed line is skipped with a counted warning, not a crash
- Offline fixture: a tiny committed slice of the dump under tests/fixtures/ drives the tests; no network
- Tests pass (pytest)
- Lint passes (ruff)
- Type checks pass (mypy)

tasks.title: T9-US-002: A `wikidata-dump` source adapter with SPARQL parity
tasks.description:
As a curator, I want a category to source its entities from the local dump instead of the live Query Service, with no change to anything downstream.

Acceptance criteria (all must be met before marking complete):
- A new `wikidata-dump` source.type, registered in the adapter factory, whose category selects entities by class membership (P31, optionally P279* transitive) over the streamed dump and yields the same RawRecord shape as the wikidata-sparql adapter
- A category can switch between `wikidata-sparql` and `wikidata-dump` for the same class with identical downstream normalization, linking, and export
- Parity test: the same fixture class resolved via a stubbed SPARQL response and via the fixture dump yields equivalent rows (same QIDs, names)
- Documented in docs/acquisition.md alongside the other adapters (required spec fields, when to use it)
- Tests pass (pytest)
- Lint passes (ruff)
- Type checks pass (mypy)

tasks.title: T9-US-003: Rich entity hydration from the dump
tasks.description:
As a data curator, I want dump-sourced nodes to carry far more than a label and image, so the corpus is richer than what the lightweight SPARQL SELECTs return.

Acceptance criteria (all must be met before marking complete):
- The dump adapter extracts a configurable set of statements/qualifiers per entity (e.g. inception, location, country of origin, material, derived-from/influenced-by, coordinates, multilingual labels) into the canonical schema's columns and provenance, not just label+image
- The property-to-column mapping is declarative (per-domain or shared config), so adding an attribute does not require code changes
- Hydrated values feed the existing dimension columns the ontology linkers read (temporal/geographic/linguistic/genetic), so richer input produces more links — verified on the fixture
- Tests pass (pytest)
- Lint passes (ruff)
- Type checks pass (mypy)

tasks.title: T9-US-004: On-disk class-membership index over the dump
tasks.description:
As an operator, I want a prebuilt index so large classes resolve fast on repeated runs instead of rescanning the whole dump each time.

Acceptance criteria (all must be met before marking complete):
- A one-pass indexer builds an on-disk index from the dump mapping QID -> classes (P31 / P279*) and class -> member QIDs
- The `wikidata-dump` adapter uses the index when present (fast class membership) and falls back to a full scan when it is absent, with identical results
- The index records the dump version/date it was built from and is rejected (with a clear message) if pointed at a different dump
- Built and queried entirely offline against the fixture dump slice in tests
- Tests pass (pytest)
- Lint passes (ruff)
- Type checks pass (mypy)

tasks.title: T9-US-005: Dump-backed enrichment pass for existing corpora
tasks.description:
As an analyst, I want to enrich an already-scraped corpus from the local dump using each node's wikidata_qid, so SPARQL-sourced data gains the dump's depth without rescraping.

Acceptance criteria (all must be met before marking complete):
- A step (CLI subcommand or pipeline stage) that, given a canonical TSV corpus whose nodes carry wikidata_qid, looks each entity up in the dump and fills missing attributes (multilingual names -> NAMED_IN, coordinates/place -> geographic, inception -> temporal, derived-from/influenced-by -> genetic), feeding the existing ontology linkers
- Enrichment is provenance-aware and idempotent: it records that a value came from the dump (with the dump version) and never clobbers a higher-confidence existing value
- Only registered :TYPEs and valid dimensions are produced; metrics show the added links
- Verified offline on a fixture corpus + fixture dump slice
- Tests pass (pytest)
- Lint passes (ruff)
- Type checks pass (mypy)

tasks.title: T9-US-006: Document the dump workflow, provenance, and an offline smoke test
tasks.description:
As a maintainer, I want the bulk-dump path documented and guarded end to end so it ships trustworthy and stays reproducible.

Acceptance criteria (all must be met before marking complete):
- A docs page (docs/sources-wikidata.md or an extension of docs/acquisition.md) explains obtaining and refreshing the Wikidata dump, building the index, the `wikidata-dump` source.type, hydration config, and the enrichment step
- Dump version/date is recorded in run provenance so a corpus says which dump it came from
- An offline smoke test exercises fetch -> normalize -> validate for a `wikidata-dump` category against the fixture dump slice and asserts expected rows and links
- PLAN.md and README reflect that Wikidata is the primary raw-data backbone and that bulk-dump ingestion is supported; the locked-decisions note about structured-first acquisition is updated accordingly
- Tests pass (pytest)
- Lint passes (ruff)
- Type checks pass (mypy)
